reasons: Both answers explain why heap-only -Xmx exceeds the container limit, separate the OOM kill from a Java OutOfMemoryError, recommend MaxRAMPercentage with a higher limit or smaller heap, and give NMT and kubectl measurement commands in Russian. B adds useful extras (the Mi/m equivalence, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, verification steps) but turns on aggressive per-area caps by default and slightly overstates the working_set metric's role for the kernel OOM killer. A is more cautious, making those caps optional and conditional on NMT, so neither is clearly better.

B: Claims the kernel OOM killer compares container_memory_working_set_bytes against the limit; the cgroup OOM killer acts on cgroup memory usage, while working_set is what kubelet uses for eviction (minor imprecision).
